acceptanceCriteria: `impact --base` emits, per changed declaration, its referencing sites and covering tests with syntax-level confidence and an explicit unknown for unresolved references.
A fixture shows a changed function whose importers do not reference it excluded from the symbol-level set but kept in the import-level set.
Measured on the frozen corpus against the import-level result before any default change.
body: Filed 2026-09-27 from the owner-requested gap analysis of Corvint against competing context tools, current standards and a trial on a local clone of MeVille (TypeScript, about 4,600 tracked files). `impact` is import-level for Go, Python and JS/TS, with caller edges only for Go (internal/contextindex/impact_callers.go). Competitors map a diff to changed symbols, then to callers and affected tests (codebase-memory detect_changes, Greptile, CodeRabbit, Qodo). The identifier graph exists but is off by default because it regressed recall@20 (decision 0367, V1-0185); that concerns ranking, not diff impact. A changed-declaration set from the diff hunks, joined to identifier references, gives a narrower and explainable blast radius than whole-file reverse imports.
title: impact: symbol-level diff impact from changed declarations to referencing sites and tests
